headline: Agentic Coding's Blind Spot: Knowing What Your Agents Are Doing
summary: This piece examines the growing reliance on AI coding agents to autonomously write and ship code, and argues that engineers still need deep technical literacy to review, debug, and trust agent-generated work. It explores where human oversight remains non-negotiable even as agents take on more of the implementation burden.
why_it_matters: As you build LLM applications on ServiceNow and move toward an AI Application Engineer role, this directly addresses a core skill you'll need: knowing how much to trust agentic output versus when to dig into the internals yourself. It's a useful framework for designing review processes around agent-driven development.

headline: LEANN Slashes RAG Vector Index Size by 97% Without Sacrificing Recall
summary: Researchers introduced LEANN, an open-source vector indexing method accepted at MLSys 2026, that compresses a 60-million-chunk RAG index from 201GB down to just 6GB by using graph-based recomputation instead of storing full embeddings, while maintaining retrieval accuracy.
why_it_matters: For LLM application work involving retrieval-augmented generation, this kind of storage efficiency is a game-changer for deploying RAG systems in resource-constrained or enterprise environments like ServiceNow instances, where infrastructure costs and scalability matter a lot.

headline: New 27B Open Model Targets Smarter Multimodal Routing Decisions
summary: vLLM's Semantic Router project released d3-ultra, a 27-billion parameter open multimodal decision model designed to intelligently route queries across different models or tools based on content type and complexity.
why_it_matters: Semantic routing is increasingly relevant to building efficient multi-model LLM pipelines — a practical concern when designing cost-effective, production-grade AI applications rather than relying on a single large model for every task.

headline: OpenAI Cuts Agent API Costs in Half with GPT-6.1 Terra Launch
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra and simultaneously halved the API pricing for GPT-6.1 Sol, specifically targeting cost reduction for agentic workloads that make repeated or chained API calls.
why_it_matters: Lower API costs for agent-style workloads directly affects the economics of building and scaling LLM-powered applications, making it more feasible to deploy agentic features in enterprise tools like ServiceNow without prohibitive inference costs.

headline: Why KV Cache Management Is the Secret to Scaling LLM Inference
summary: This technical presentation breaks down how key-value (KV) cache strategies are central to serving large language models efficiently at scale, covering memory management techniques that reduce latency and cost in production inference systems.
why_it_matters: Understanding KV cache optimization is foundational knowledge for anyone deploying LLMs in production — it's the kind of systems-level engineering detail that separates a working prototype from a scalable AI application, directly relevant to your career trajectory.
